pr_body:
This fixes both big and small issues with the OSSL_DESERIALIZER library code:

1.  The passphrase handling was modelled after OSSL_SERIALIZER, which is all about encryption and that the caller must specify the cipher to use...  but with deserialization being about *de*cryption and that the necessary info comes with the serialized input, this needed to be redone.
2.  Deserializers for all our asymmetric keys are now added, and can handle public keys too.  `test/serdes_test.c` has been modified to test them all.
3.  Refactored the constructor setting functions, and most of all renamed "finalizer" to "constructor" (thanks @t8m, sorry that I lost that in #12410).
4.  Made the deserialization use purely BIO_tell() and BIO_seek() for file rewind...  BIO_reset() is hard to use generically.  (fixes #12541)


Additionally, there were a few small fixes in other parts of libcrypto.

issue_context.title: OSSL_DESERIALIZER_from_bio not working with file bio
comments:
I've found that BIO_reset() is not very usable in many cases, so it's probably better to switch to pure BIO_tell() / BIO_seek() use. BIO_s_mem can easily be modified to support that (since we use that internally).

A point here is that it should be possible to have more than object in the same file, especially PEM, so OSSL_DESERIALIZER_from_bio() needs to be able to deal with that. 

I have a PR coming up soon that deals with this and more.
Thank you. Please also see the new issue: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/issues/12568
